title: Redis Configuration
description: Listener, memory, persistence and security settings for the single-node server.

port.title: Port
port.description: Listener port. Keep in sync with the service port on the deployment.

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: Data memory cap and what the server does when it is reached.

maxmemory.title: Max Memory
maxmemory.description: Cap for data, e.g. 256mb or 1gb. Keep below the workload memory limit; Redis needs headroom during snapshots.

maxmemory_policy.title: Max Memory Policy
maxmemory_policy.description: Behaviour at the cap. noeviction fails writes; allkeys-lru suits cache-style usage.

persistence.title: Persistence
persistence.description: On-disk durability on the redis-data volume.

appendonly.title: Append-Only File (AOF)
appendonly.description: Adds AOF on top of the default RDB snapshots: better durability, more disk and I/O.

security.title: Security
security.description: Authentication and transport encryption. TLS is exclusive: it disables the plaintext listener and Port becomes the TLS port.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: PASSWORD requires AUTH; TLS encrypts the listener.

extra_args.title: Extra Arguments
extra_args.description: Extra redis-server arguments appended verbatim, e.g. --loglevel debug. They are appended last and therefore override the managed settings above (that is how --tls-auth-clients yes works, but it also means --requirepass '' or --port disables the security settings). Split on whitespace only: quotes are kept as literal characters, so arguments containing spaces or empty-string values such as --save '' cannot be expressed here. Do not set --dir; it is pinned to the persistent volume.
